texto:
Benchmark campaign goal is a dimension in Amazon Ads unified reporting that records which campaign objective Amazon used when it compared a campaign with its peers. A benchmark only means something if the comparison is like for like: a campaign built to win top-of-search visibility should not be judged against campaigns built to drive purchases. The field exists so that anyone reading a benchmark row can see which goal bucket the peer figures came from. Amazon's dimensions reference, updated on November 11, 2026, describes the field as derived "from campaign goal and optimization settings," according to PPC Land's analysis of the 156 unified report dimensions.
Where the field sits
Amazon's unified reporting, which replaces the separate Sponsored Ads and Amazon DSP (demand-side platform) report sets, organises its attributes into 11 categories. One of them is Benchmark, with seven attributes: benchmark brand ID, benchmark brand name, benchmark browse category ID, benchmark browse category path, benchmark browse category level, benchmark browse category marketplace and benchmark campaign goal.
Six of the seven describe the brand and the shopping category, and are "derived from the products promoted in the campaign," according to the Amazon reference as reported by PPC Land. Benchmark campaign goal is the odd one out. It describes the campaign itself rather than the products. Together the seven fields define the peer group: the brand being compared, the Amazon browse category it competes in, the marketplace and the objective.
The field is a text dimension, not a metric: it groups rows so the benchmark columns beside it can be read against the right comparison set. PPC Land's count of Amazon's product icons shows all seven benchmark attributes marked for DVA+ (Amazon's display, video and audio campaign type), Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and Sponsored Display. Where an attribute does not apply to a campaign's ad product, Amazon says the value "appears as null."
How it gets its value
The advertiser does not type a benchmark campaign goal. Amazon assigns it from two inputs on the campaign: the goal chosen at creation and the optimisation settings underneath.
Those inputs differ by ad product, which is why a derivation is needed. Sponsored Brands has carried explicit goals since October 25, 2023. Drive page visits is billed per click (CPC, cost per click), serves on search results, product detail pages and the home page, and treats clicks as its success measure. Grow brand impression share is billed per thousand viewable impressions (vCPM), serves only at the top of search results and measures success by top-of-search impression share, according to Amazon's launch note.
Sponsored Display campaigns are built around an optimisation goal. For most of the product's life the options were reach, page visits and conversions. On April 4, 2025 Amazon moved active reach and page visit campaigns to the conversion objective.
DVA+, announced on September 29, 2026, starts with an objective: sales, leads, subscriptions, traffic or awareness, according to Amazon's DVA+ guide. Beneath that, Amazon routes the campaign to one of two optimisation engines, Brand+ for awareness and reach or Performance+ for conversion goals measured by cost per acquisition. Amazon DSP's goal-based bidding, launched in October 2023, labels its creation screens "Performance (CPA) Goals" and "Brand (Reach) Goals."
Sponsored Products is the hard case. It has no goal picker comparable to Sponsored Brands, so any goal must come from the optimisation settings, such as the bidding strategy. Amazon has not published how it maps those settings to a benchmark goal.
As of November 2026 Amazon has not published the list of values benchmark campaign goal can take. The benchmark launch pages from November 2025 and May 2026 say only that advertisers can filter benchmarks by "ad formats and campaign goals."
How it is used in a report
The benchmark dimensions are optional. Amazon's Support Center page "Understanding benchmark metrics and recommended actions," updated on November 11, 2026, names benchmark brand name, benchmark browse category path and benchmark campaign goal as dimensions that can be added to a report to show "the peer group for each comparison," as reported by PPC Land's review of the 16 recommended actions.
A worked example shows the logic. A brand runs two Sponsored Brands campaigns in the same category, one on Drive page visits and one on Grow brand impression share. In a report broken out by benchmark campaign goal, each campaign's CTR (click-through rate) sits on its own row with three peer columns beside it: CTR (p25), CTR (p50) and CTR (p75), the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the peer group. The impression-share campaign, which buys top-of-search slots on a vCPM basis, is compared with other impression-share campaigns, not with click-optimised ones.
Eight metrics carry benchmarks: percent of purchases new to brand, purchase rate (new to brand), cost per purchase (new to brand), CTR, CPC, CPM (cost per thousand impressions), video completion rate and cost per completed view. The campaign manager insight card shows only the median. The 25th and 75th percentiles appear in unified reporting and the Reporting API.
Through the API, benchmarks arrive as two report types: crossProgramBenchmarks for sponsored ads and dspBenchmarks for the DSP side, now DVA.
Origin and evolution
Amazon has offered peer comparisons since at least January 28, 2021, when it launched the Sponsored Brands category benchmark report. That report showed impressions, CTR, return on ad spend (ROAS) and advertising cost of sales (ACOS) at the median and upper and lower quartiles of "your closest peers" within shopping categories, over a 90-day lookback.
The current product launched in beta in the United States on November 18, 2025. Amazon presented it as self-service benchmarks across ad formats and campaign goals, for Brand Registry owners and endemic advertisers. On March 27, 2026, Amazon promoted a white paper describing the method. Peer groups, which it calls PeerSets, are built using K-nearest-neighbour matching on brand revenue and average selling price within a category, supplemented by a large language model that assesses competition and customer overlap. No single brand may contribute more than 49% of the weight, and at least five peer brands are required, according to PPC Land's summary of the paper.
General availability followed on May 18, 2026 in 18 countries, PPC Land reported. The November 11, 2026 dimensions reference is the first Amazon document PPC Land found that lists benchmark campaign goal as a named unified reporting attribute.
Why it matters
The goal label decides what "good" looks like. Amazon's recommended actions turn a benchmark position into advice, so a campaign placed in the wrong goal group receives the wrong advice. A Sponsored Brands impression-share campaign judged against click-optimised peers would probably show a weak CTR and an elevated CPC, which Amazon's table answers with prompts to "Test new ad copies, improve keyword relevancy."
It also matters for agencies and tool vendors pulling API data. Legacy reports become read-only on December 17, 2026 and shut down on January 31, 2027. PPC Land noted that the scheduled-report migration page listed the benchmark report among ten types not yet available in unified reporting as of November 12, 2026.
Limitations and disputes
The first problem is opacity. A field "derived from campaign goal and optimization settings" cannot be audited if the derivation rules and the value list are unpublished.
Second, the method itself is contested. Amazon's help page says benchmarks use "ad-spend weighted calculations" yet describes the median as the point where "half of peer brands perform above and half perform below." PPC Land argued that a spend-weighted median splits spend, not brands, and showed a three-brand case where an unweighted median CTR of 10% becomes a weighted median of 3.00%.
Third, product coverage is inconsistent. The dimensions table marks the benchmark fields for Sponsored Display, but the November help page says benchmark metrics are available for "Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Streaming TV, and DVA+," leaving Sponsored Display out. The May 2026 announcement included it.
Fourth, the advice attached to benchmarks leans one way. All eight favourable cells in Amazon's table recommend scaling, investing or bidding higher, and none suggests cutting a budget. That reading carries extra weight after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 22 states sued Amazon on August 31, 2026 over auction pricing; the complaint alleges advertisers paid their full bid 79% of the time. Amazon denies the allegations.
Commonly confused terms
Campaign goal vs benchmark campaign goal. The campaign goal is the setting the advertiser chooses at creation. The benchmark campaign goal is Amazon's classification of that campaign for peer comparison, which can draw on optimisation settings as well, and may group differently.
Campaign bid strategy. A separate unified reporting dimension describing how bids are set. It is one possible input to the benchmark goal, not the goal itself.
Ad group optimization type. A separate ad group-level dimension describing what an ad group optimises toward, not the peer group.
Benchmark browse category. The category fields define where a brand competes. The goal field defines what the campaign is trying to do. Both are needed to identify a peer group.
Recent developments
The field entered the public record with Amazon's November 11, 2026 updates to its dimensions reference and benchmark help page. A further change could move benchmark positions soon: from January 1, 2027, DVA display ads on the Amazon Store will count impressions only when on screen, and Amazon expects 63% fewer impressions on average. PPC Land estimated that a campaign with unchanged spend and clicks would see CPM and CTR both rise about 2.7 times, which could shift its standing against peers.
Timeline
- January 28, 2021 - Amazon launches the Sponsored Brands category benchmark report, comparing impressions, CTR, ROAS and ACOS with category peers over 90 days.
- October 25, 2023 - Sponsored Brands introduces goal-based campaigns (Drive page visits, Grow brand impression share); Amazon DSP adds goal-based bidding.
- April 4, 2025 - Amazon moves active Sponsored Display reach and page visit campaigns to the conversion objective.
- November 11, 2025 - Unified reporting enters beta at unBoxed.
- November 18, 2025 - Self-service benchmarks launch in beta in the US, filterable by ad format and campaign goal, with crossProgramBenchmarks and dspBenchmarks API reports.
- March 27, 2026 - Amazon promotes its benchmarks white paper describing KNN and LLM peer matching.
- May 18, 2026 - Benchmarks reach general availability in 18 countries.
- June 8, 2026 - Unified reporting reaches general availability.
- September 29, 2026 - Amazon DSP renamed DVA; DVA+ announced with five objectives.
- November 11, 2026 - Amazon's dimensions reference lists seven benchmark attributes, including benchmark campaign goal; benchmark help page updated.
- December 17, 2026 - Legacy reporting pages scheduled to become read-only.
- January 1, 2027 - On-screen impression counting begins for DVA display on the Amazon Store.
- January 31, 2027 - Legacy reports scheduled to shut down.

Summary
Who: Amazon Ads defines and populates the field. It is read by brand owners and representatives registered in Brand Registry, endemic advertisers, agencies and reporting tools using the Amazon Ads Reporting API.
What: Benchmark campaign goal is one of seven benchmark dimensions in Amazon's unified reporting. It labels the campaign objective Amazon used to place a campaign in a peer group, so that benchmark percentiles for metrics such as CTR, CPC and CPM are compared within the same goal. Amazon derives it from the campaign goal and optimisation settings, and has not published its value list.
When: Benchmarks filterable by campaign goal launched in beta on November 18, 2025 and reached general availability on May 18, 2026. The field appears as a named unified reporting attribute in Amazon's dimensions reference updated on November 11, 2026.
Where: In Amazon Ads unified reporting and the Reporting API, for campaigns across DVA+, Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands and, according to the dimensions table, Sponsored Display, in 18 countries.
Why: Campaigns built for different objectives produce different metrics, so a benchmark is only meaningful within one goal. The field makes the comparison group visible, though Amazon's unpublished derivation rules and weighting method leave the comparison hard to verify.
